The `toClass(Object[])` method in `org.apache.commons.lang3.ClassUtils` takes an array of objects as input, gets the class of each object in the array, and returns an array of `Class` objects. It handles cases where the input array is null by returning null and where it is empty by returning an empty class array.

From the failing test `testToClass_object()`, it seems that the test is asserting that the result of `ClassUtils.toClass(new Object[] { "Test", null, 99d })` should be an array containing the classes `String.class`, `null`, and `Double.class`.

The current bug report mentions that `toClass(Object[])` throws a NullPointerException on a null array element.

Let's analyze the `toClass(Object[])` method to see if we can identify the root cause of the NullPointerException.
The `toClass(Object[])` method in `org.apache.commons.lang3.ClassUtils` iterates over each element in the input array and retrieves the class of the element using the `getClass()` method. However, if any element in the input array is null, calling `getClass()` on a null object will result in a NullPointerException.

In the failing test `testToClass_object()`, the input array contains a null element (`null`), which leads to the NullPointerException when trying to retrieve the class of that null element.

To fix this issue and avoid the NullPointerException, we need to add a null check before calling `getClass()` on each element in the input array in the `toClass(Object[])` method.

The method that needs to be fixed is:
`org.apache.commons.lang3.ClassUtils.toClass(java.lang.Object[])`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
